header: Date: 2026-12-15 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alice Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Soto (Redwood SE), Rina Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (HelioWorks Head of Platform), Dan Liu (SRE), Karen Patel (Lead ML), Omar Hassan (Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rehearsal for production cutover. Reviewed canary traffic plan, circuit-breaker thresholds, monitoring/alerting mappings and runbook playbacks. Key risks: KMS rotation timing, canary perf regression under burst traffic, and routing fallbacks. Agreed next steps to tighten runbook and run one staged chaos test in staging.
topics: Cutover sequencing, Canary split and A/B gating, circuit-breaker thresholds, observability dashboards, alert routing, rollback commands, security/KMS checks, runbook dry-run and decision timing.
attachments: Links: 1) Cutover Runbook draft - https://redwood.link/helioworks-cutover 2) Canary metrics dashboard - https://dash.redwood/helioworks/canary 3) Security pack (SOC2 excerpt + KMS notes) - https://redwood.link/sec-brief
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Park: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 48 minutes, main goals are to walk the cutover runbook and validate circuit breaker thresholds and obs handoff. hi Priya, Dan, Karen.
[00:18] Priya Nair: hi, thanks. we've got leadership on standby, want to make sure the rollback path is explicit, last time there was some ambiguity around the canary switchback.
[00:27] Miguel Soto: yeah so we'll show the routing matrix, it has the canary at 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100, and we recommend a step at 5% for latency and error checks.
[00:36] Dan Liu: quick question, that 5% hold — how long is the soak? we need numbers to align with SLO windows.
[00:42] Alice Park: good call. proposal in runbook is a 10 minute soak at 5% with automated checks against p50/p95 and error rate. if error rate delta > 0.5% then circuit trip.
[00:54] Karen Patel: 10 minutes might be okay but for large models p95 variance is noisy; can we also check token-level hallucination rate against our eval prompts?
[01:05] Miguel Soto: we can add the eval prompt regression as a gating check — we have a lightweight eval harness. It runs in parallel and reports a pass/fail boolean.
[01:12] Priya Nair: perfect, add that. also need the canary to atomically switch model variant if perf regresses, not manual.
[01:20] Alice Park: yep automation is in scope — we have a fallback route to a quantized variant we call rwd-quant-compat in the config. heads up, sometimes transcription/notes show it as ‘red wood quant’.
[01:30] Omar Hassan: on security, KMS rotation window — can the Greenwood keys (sic) be kept out of the cutover window? we can't rotate keys during go-live.
[01:38] Alice Park: yes, good flag. we'll document explicit KMS freeze window in the runbook. Miguel can share the KMS rotation doc link.
[01:45] Miguel Soto: sharing now in chat. note, for private deployment customers the key management integration differs slightly — we outline both in section 4.
[01:55] Dan Liu: alarms — need to know who gets paged at 3x error rate and who gets paged at 10% traffic drop. we can't have the wrong team paged.
[02:04] Rina Kapoor: we'll map alert names to your on-call rota; can you provide the rota csv?
[02:09] Dan Liu: yes I'll upload after this call.
[02:12] [00:02:12] Karen Patel: can I ask about load spikes? we saw a burst in staging yesterday that elongated p95 by 300ms, thought it might be KV cache warmup.
[02:23] Miguel Soto: KV cache warmup is common; runbook has a cache-warm phase: pre-warm cache with historical prefixes for 15 minutes and run a small synthetic traffic set. if you can't pre-warm then the circuit-breaker thresholds should be relaxed for the first 20 minutes.
[02:38] Priya Nair: we prefer pre-warm, but what if we don't have historical user prefixes for a new segment?
[02:45] Miguel Soto: fallback is to use prefix-sim generator that we provide; it creates synthetic prefixes representative of your expected distribution. results are not perfect but reduce first-token jitter.
[02:55] Alice Park: action item: Miguel to add prefix generator steps to runbook.
[03:00] [00:03:00] Dan Liu: on the observability handoff — who will own the dashboard alerts in the first 72 hours?
[03:07] Priya Nair: Platform will own paging, Redwood will own model perf investigation and fallback action. we want a clear escalation to Redwood SE if model error exceeds threshold.
[03:17] Miguel Soto: confirm — Redwood will have on-call contact and we will be reachable via the pager duty integration. we'll also provide a Slack channel for real-time handoffs.
[03:27] Karen Patel: about A/B experiments — we plan an A/B at 10% of traffic to validate latency vs quality tradeoff. what's the best practice to measure quality without labeling?
[03:36] Miguel Soto: use embedding-based similarity on a held-out prompt set, and the eval harness can compute a quality score proxy. it's not a human label but it's deterministic and fast.
[03:46] Priya Nair: ok we want both the proxy and a small human review sample from the top 100 queries.
[03:53] Alice Park: noted. that will be added to the gate checklist.
[03:58] [00:03:58] Dan Liu: what about rollback time budget? we need an SLA on rollback completion if canary trips.
[04:05] Alice Park: the runbook sets rollback target at 5 minutes to reroute traffic and 10 minutes to redeploy a stable variant. those are target times, we'll stress test them.
[04:15] Dan Liu: 5 minutes seems aggressive but acceptable if automation works. we'll validate.
[04:20] Miguel Soto: some caveat — large KV caches can take longer to purge; our fallback is to route to a smaller quantized model that requires no KV priming. that reduces user impact.
[04:33] [00:04:33] Karen Patel: can you spell out the commands so our ops folks can do manual rollback if automation fails?
[04:40] Alice Park: yes the runbook has explicit CLI commands and a one-click button in the console. we'll keep both.
[04:47] Priya Nair: security question — will audit logs include token-level metadata? we need to confirm PII redaction.
[04:55] Omar Hassan: we only accept metadata-level logs in our environment, token text redaction is required. how does Redwood handle that?
[05:02] Miguel Soto: by default we redact user prompt text in hosted mode, but for dedicated/private we can configure redaction and forward only non-PII telemetry. the security pack we shared details this.
[05:12] [00:05:12] Priya Nair: excellent. can you add a short checklist for compliance sign-off?
[05:18] Rina Kapoor: will do, add to runbook section 7.
[05:22] Karen Patel: one more — throttling and rate limits during cutover. if we ramp to 20% and then 100% quickly, do we have automatic throttles?
[05:31] Miguel Soto: yes, we have traffic shaping rules and token-bucket throttles at the ingress. the runbook includes safe ramp rates. if thresholds hit, circuit trips and traffic reverts to baseline.
[05:41] [00:05:41] Priya Nair: let's talk about the actual rehearsal timeline — what do you propose for a dry-run?
[05:47] Alice Park: propose this schedule: T-48h decision call; T-24h config freeze; T-2h quiet window; T-0 perform cutover; T+1h monitoring; T+24h post-mortem. Dry-run tomorrow in staging will execute the same timeline with synthetic traffic.
[06:02] Dan Liu: we want the dry-run to include a simulated KMS rotation to ensure we don't break keys during cutover.
[06:08] Miguel Soto: we can simulate rotation by toggling a dummy key in staging, yes.
[06:12] [00:06:12] Karen Patel: can you also measure cold-start token cost for the quantized fallback? we need to model cost impact of frequent fallbacks.
[06:20] Alice Park: Miguel will provide cost delta numbers for fallback vs baseline.
[06:24] Miguel Soto: will include in the updated runbook and send a small perf spreadsheet.
[06:30] Priya Nair: regarding A/B gating, if the A variant wins on quality but loses on latency, what do we do?
[06:37] Alice Park: decision policy in runbook: prioritize SLO compliance first; if latency delta is within agreed tolerance then allow quality preference, otherwise fallback to latency-preserving variant. we'll capture the tolerance numbers in the decision matrix.
[06:50] [00:06:50] Dan Liu: slight tangent — any competitor tech we should be mindful of? we heard some folks evaluate Anthropic for low-latency demos.
[06:57] Miguel Soto: Anthropic was mentioned, but their managed path still requires heavy instrumentation for canary automation; our value is the orchestration and rollback primitives.
[07:07] Karen Patel: good.
[07:10] [00:07:10] Alice Park: ok let's do a live walkthrough of the runbook, Miguel?
[07:14] Miguel Soto: sure. opening runbook, section 2 shows pre-cutover checks: schema validation, key rotation freeze, infra capacity checks. note the capacity check has a canary-per-GPU guideline.
[07:27] Dan Liu: what's the GPU headroom requirement?
[07:30] Miguel Soto: recommend 30% headroom at baseline to handle transient surges; if you can't commit, we'll accept a lower headroom but then lower the step sizes in the traffic ramp.
[07:40] Priya Nair: we can target 25% headroom, but we'll run a stress test next week.
[07:46] [00:07:46] Karen Patel: Miguel, when you talk about node autoscale, does the autoscaler respect the scaling cool-down during cutover? we can't have nodes flapping mid-ramp.
[07:55] Miguel Soto: runbook suggests disabling autoscale for the 2h window around cutover and using manual scale steps; we include commands for that.
[08:02] Alice Park: adding that to the runbook checklist.
[08:06] [00:08:06] Priya Nair: any telemetry gating thresholds you recommend for the first 24h?
[08:11] Miguel Soto: p95 latency > 2x baseline or error delta > 1% triggers immediate partial rollback to 20% traffic. full rollback if sustained for > 10m.
[08:20] Dan Liu: are these thresholds customizable?
[08:22] Alice Park: yes, we treat them as config per customer. we'll work with you to tune them during the pilot.
[08:29] [00:08:29] Karen Patel: quick note, last week's bench had a small regression when sequences hit 1k tokens. can we set a sequence-length cap for the canary?
[08:37] Miguel Soto: yes cap at 512 tokens for canary traffic to reduce variance; full traffic can go up to 2k after stable.
[08:44] Priya Nair: that helps.
[08:47] [00:08:47] Alice Park: ok, near the end here, recap of owners: Alice will update runbook and share; Miguel will run 1% canary perf test and share spreadsheet; Dan will provide rota CSV; Omar will confirm KMS compliance gaps.
[09:02] Rina Kapoor: I'll create the decision-call invite for T-48h.
[09:06] [00:09:06] Priya Nair: thanks all. one last ask — can Redwood run the rehearsal with one of your engineers shadowing our on-call? we'd like live support.
[09:15] Miguel Soto: yes we'll schedule a shift. I'll coordinate with Rina.
[09:20] Alice Park: great. any other risks?
[09:23] Dan Liu: none from my side.
[09:25] Karen Patel: all good.
[09:27] Alice Park: closing — I'll send updated runbook and the perf sheet. meeting adjourned.
[09:30] [00:09:30] End of recording.
